title: Unwanted
subtitle: Unwanted 可以表示『不再想要、不需要、數量過多、不受歡迎、已棄置、功能多餘、已過時，或已進入處置流程』。 這些原因不能混為一談。替換前要先判斷：Is it unwanted
description: Unwanted 可以表示『不再想要、不需要、數量過多、不受歡迎、已棄置、功能多餘、已過時，或已進入處置流程』。 這些原因不能混為一談。替換前要先判斷：Is it unwanted because of preference, lack of need, excess quantity, redundancy, obsolescence, or disposal status?

words.meaning: 不再需要的；不再想要的

exercises.original: The shop collects unwanted clothes for charity.
exercises.zh: 商店收集不再需要的衣物作慈善用途。

options.explanation: No longer desired ✓ — previously wanted or useful but not wanted any more. Here, owners no longer want the items. That makes No longer desired the most precise replacement for this particular sense of unwanted.

Unneeded — not required for a particular purpose. This focuses on lack of necessity, not desire, excess quantity, disposal status, or obsolescence. The decisive clue is that owners no longer want the items.
Surplus — more than is needed or required. This specifically means more than is needed and is too quantity-focused elsewhere. The decisive clue is that owners no longer want the items.
Unused — not currently used. Something can be unused but still wanted or valuable. The decisive clue is that owners no longer want the items.
Old — not new. Age alone does not mean an item is unwanted. The decisive clue is that owners no longer want the items.
Broken — damaged and not functioning properly. Damage is a condition and does not tell us whether the item is wanted. The decisive clue is that owners no longer want the items.

exercises.zh: 員工必須在收集前登記所有待處置設備。
exercises.upgrade: Staff must record all items to be disposed of before collection.

options.explanation: Discarded — thrown away or abandoned because no longer wanted or useful. This says disposal has already happened and is too strong if the item is merely unwanted. The decisive clue is that administrative disposal procedure is explicit.

Items to be disposed of ✓ — items formally identified for removal, disposal, or recycling. Here, administrative disposal procedure is explicit. That makes Items to be disposed of the most precise replacement for this particular sense of unwanted.
Surplus — more than is needed or required. This specifically means more than is needed and is too quantity-focused elsewhere. The decisive clue is that administrative disposal procedure is explicit.
Unused — not currently used. Something can be unused but still wanted or valuable. The decisive clue is that administrative disposal procedure is explicit.
Old — not new. Age alone does not mean an item is unwanted. The decisive clue is that administrative disposal procedure is explicit.
Broken — damaged and not functioning properly. Damage is a condition and does not tell us whether the item is wanted. The decisive clue is that administrative disposal procedure is explicit.

exercises.original: The audit identified unwanted assets for removal.
exercises.zh: 審計識別需要移除的待處置資產。
exercises.upgrade: The audit identified items to be disposed of for removal.

falseSynonyms.zh: 未使用 ≠ unwanted unused 只表示沒有使用，可能仍然想保留。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Unused does not mean unwanted.

falseSynonyms.zh: 不受歡迎 ≠ unwanted unpopular 主要指很多人不喜歡，不是某人不再需要。
損壞 ≠ unwanted broken 物品可能仍然想修理或保留。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Broken describes condition, not desirability.

falseSynonyms.zh: 舊 ≠ unwanted old 只是年齡／時間狀態，不等於不想要。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Old does not necessarily mean unwanted.

falseSynonyms.zh: 只在已丟棄 sense 接近 discarded 表示處置已發生。
只在數量過多 sense 接近 surplus 是因為超出需要，不等於任何 unwanted item。
只在功能多餘 sense 接近 redundant 常表示功能被取代或重複。
詞形陷阱 unwanted 是形容詞；unwantedly 極少用且不自然。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Use unwanted mainly as an adjective.
